questions.text: Let ABC be a triangle such that $\angle \mathrm{ACB}=\frac{\pi}{6}$ and let $\mathrm{a}, \mathrm{b}$ and c denote the lengths of the sides opposite to A , $B$ and $C$ respectively. The value(s) of $x$ for which $a=x^{2}+x+1, b=x^{2}-1$ and $c=2 x+1$ is (are)

options.D:
$4 \sqrt{3}$

Sol. (B)
Using cosine rule for $\angle \mathrm{C}$
$$\begin{array}{l}
\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}=\frac{\left(x^{2}+x+1\right)^{2}+\left(x^{2}-1\right)^{2}-(2 x+1)^{2}}{2\left(x^{2}+x+1\right)\left(x^{2}-1\right)} \\
\Rightarrow \sqrt{3}=\frac{2 x^{2}+2 x-1}{x^{2}+x+1} \\
\Rightarrow(\sqrt{3}-2) x^{2}+(\sqrt{3}-2) x+(\sqrt{3}+1)=0 \\
\Rightarrow x=\frac{(2-\sqrt{3}) \pm \sqrt{3}}{2(\sqrt{3}-2)} \\
\Rightarrow x=-(2+\sqrt{3}), 1+\sqrt{3} \Rightarrow x=1+\sqrt{3} \text { as }(x>0)
\end{array}$$
